core_obligations: Set up the combinatorics (proof lines 3778-3791): choose an affine open covering indexed by a set I and affine open coverings of the pairwise intersections indexed by sets I_ij, and let kappa be an infinite cardinal at least the cardinality of all those index sets.

Define a refinement operation on families of subsets (proof lines 3793-3818): for each index and each element of a module of sections choose a finite subset of another module expressing its image under base change as a finite sum; for a family of subsets of cardinality at most kappa define a new family by collecting all the chosen finite subsets, which again has cardinality at most kappa, and iterate to obtain a family stable under the operation; the submodules generated by the resulting families glue to a quasi-coherent subsheaf which is kappa-generated.

Conclude (proof lines 3820-3843): the kappa-generated quasi-coherent subsheaves form a directed system because the sum of two of them is again one, and every section of the module over a member of the covering lies in one of them by construction, so the natural map from the colimit of the system to the module is injective and surjective.
proof_roadmap: Choose the covering data and the cardinal bounding all the index sets involved.
Build the refinement operator on families of subsets, iterate it to stability and glue to obtain a kappa-generated subsheaf containing any prescribed family.
Note that the system of such subsheaves is directed and exhausts every section.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for any scheme X there is a cardinal kappa such that every quasi-coherent module on X is the directed colimit of its kappa-generated quasi-coherent submodules (statement lines 3771-3776). The proof (proof lines 3778-3848) chooses covering data and a suitable cardinal, defines a refinement operator on families of subsets of the modules of sections, iterates it to stability to build a kappa-generated subsheaf containing a prescribed family, and concludes that the resulting directed system exhausts the module. H3: an original cardinal-bounded closure construction, written out in full.
